name: Descartes
description: Famous quotes, Scholasticism, 4 stages, Cogito, dualism, Trademark Argument, and Descartes' legacy

questions.question: Who said 'You can never step into the same river twice'?
options: Democritus
Protagoras
Heraclitus
Socrates

questions.question: Who said 'Man is the measure of all things'?
options: Aristotle
Protagoras
Socrates
Plato

questions.question: Who said 'Nothing exists except atoms and the void'?
options: Heraclitus
Aristotle
Socrates
Democritus

questions.question: Who said 'The unexamined life is not worth living'?
options: Plato
Socrates
Aristotle
Protagoras

questions.question: Who said 'There is nothing in the mind that was not first in the senses'?
options: Plato
Descartes
Aristotle
Heraclitus

questions.question: The Latin phrase 'Cogito ergo sum' translates to which of the following?
options: I exist, therefore I think
I think, therefore I am
I doubt, therefore I know
God exists, therefore I am

questions.question: St. Augustine incorporated which philosopher's ideas into Christianity?
options: Aristotle
Descartes
Plato
Aquinas

questions.question: St. Thomas Aquinas incorporated which philosopher's ideas into Christianity, creating Scholasticism?
options: Plato
Socrates
Descartes
Aristotle

questions.question: What makes Cartesian Doubt different from ordinary Skepticism?
options: Cartesian Doubt leads to permanent uncertainty about all knowledge
Cartesian Doubt is used as a method to find an unshakeable foundation for knowledge
Cartesian Doubt rejects reason as a path to truth
Cartesian Doubt was borrowed directly from ancient Greek Skeptics

questions.question: In his Meditations, Descartes concluded that all of the following could be doubted EXCEPT:
options: The existence of the physical world
Mathematical truths like 2 + 2 = 4
The existence of his own thinking mind
The reliability of his senses

questions.question: What was Stage 1 of Descartes' philosophical method in the Meditations?
options: Establish the existence of God
Apply radical doubt to reject anything that can be questioned
Prove the existence of the external world
Define the mind as distinct from the body

questions.question: What was Stage 2 of Descartes' philosophical method?
options: Use the senses to confirm physical reality
Prove God exists through the Trademark Argument
Establish the Cogito as the one unshakeable foundation of knowledge
Define Extension as the material world

questions.question: Stage 3 of Descartes' method required him to:
options: Prove the reliability of mathematical reasoning
Establish that God exists and is good rather than a deceiver
Return to the senses as a source of knowledge
Demonstrate that the mind and body are distinct substances

questions.question: What is 'Extension' according to Descartes?
options: The mind's ability to stretch beyond its natural limits
The immaterial soul that animates the body
The material, three-dimensional, divisible physical world
The part of the brain where mind and body interact

questions.question: All of the following are characteristics of the human mind according to Descartes EXCEPT:
options: It is indivisible
It is immaterial
It possesses Extension
It is capable of free will

questions.question: The Wax Argument was used by Descartes to demonstrate which of the following?
options: The senses are the most reliable source of knowledge about the world
The mind, not the senses, grasps the true nature of physical objects
Primary and secondary qualities are equally objective properties
God ensures that our perceptions accurately match reality

questions.question: Which of the following are 'primary qualities' of objects according to Descartes?
options: Color, taste, and temperature
Sound, smell, and texture
Size, shape, motion, and number
Beauty, harmony, and proportion

questions.question: What is the Trademark Argument?
options: Descartes' argument that mathematical truth proves God's existence
The idea that we could not have conceived of a perfect God unless God had implanted that idea in us
Descartes' proof that the mind is more real than the body
The argument that language contains embedded evidence of God's existence

questions.question: The 'Cartesian Circle' refers to which problem in Descartes' philosophy?
options: His endless chain of doubt that circles back to the Cogito
Circular reasoning: God validates innate ideas, but innate ideas are only trustworthy if God exists
The problem of explaining how a round pineal gland generates linear thought
The contradiction between trusting reason while doubting the senses

questions.question: The Problem of Interaction asks which of the following?
options: How can a mechanical body have any conscious experience at all?
How can an immaterial mind causally interact with a material body?
Why do humans interact differently with animals than with machines?
How can science and religious faith be reconciled in the same system?

questions.question: Where did Descartes believe the mind and body interact?
options: The frontal lobe of the brain
The heart
The pineal gland
The nervous system distributed throughout the entire body

questions.question: Descartes' philosophy unintentionally created all of the following movements EXCEPT:
options: Modern Skepticism
Philosophical Idealism
Scientific Materialism
Scholasticism

questions.question: Knowledge that is 'a priori' is best described as:
options: Knowledge gained through sensory experience and observation
Knowledge that depends on repeated empirical testing
Knowledge that exists independent of experience and is known by reason alone
Knowledge that can only be confirmed by seeing physical evidence

questions.question: Descartes is considered a Rationalist because he believed:
options: Knowledge comes primarily from sensory experience
Religious faith is the highest form of knowledge
Reason, not the senses, is the foundation of reliable knowledge
Scientific experiment is the only true path to knowledge

questions.question: According to Descartes, animals are best described as:
options: Beings with souls but no free will
Pure machines or automatons with no consciousness
Creatures guided by both instinct and limited reason
Lower forms of the same mind-body dualism that applies to humans

questions.question: Descartes was aware that his proof of God and innate ideas committed which logical fallacy?
options: Ad hominem reasoning
False dilemma
Circular reasoning, also called Begging the Question
Straw man fallacy

questions.question: Why was the Catholic Church threatened by Descartes' Cogito?
options: It implied the universe operated without God's direct intervention
It gave individuals a foundation for their own existence independent of God or the Church
It was used to argue that animals have souls equal to humans
It directly contradicted Aquinas' version of Scholasticism

questions.question: Why did Descartes believe his Mind/Body dualism was beneficial for both religion and science?
options: It proved that God created both the mind and the physical universe directly
It gave the Church authority over the mind and soul while giving scientists authority over the physical world
It showed that faith and science were both rooted in the same mathematical reasoning
It eliminated the conflict between the Cogito and the Church's teachings about God

questions.question: Descartes believed that the human mind was:
options: Subject to the same mechanical laws as all other matter in the universe
A byproduct of complex processes in the brain
Free from the laws of mechanics that govern the material world
An illusion produced by the body's nervous system over time

questions.question: Descartes believed the soul gave life and animation to the body.
options: True, the soul is what makes the body alive and capable of movement
False, the body operates as a mechanical machine on its own without the soul animating it
True, but only in the sense that the soul occupies the pineal gland which controls the body
False, because Descartes did not believe the soul and body interacted in any way
